lines.text: Have you ever talked about buying hiking boots, and suddenly your phone shows ads for hiking boots everywhere?
It feels like your phone is eavesdropping on your vocal conversations.
Security researchers have thoroughly analyzed network packets and found apps rarely secretly stream your voice.
Modern mobile operating systems strictly require explicit microphone permissions, displaying an orange privacy dot.
The reality is far creepier: ad tracking networks don't need your microphone.
They predict your desires by combining your GPS location, browsing history, and what your nearby friends just purchased.
The predictive data algorithms are simply so frighteningly accurate that they don't even need to listen.
